key_insight: Noise-informed quantum error correction can recover strong memory and logic performance on a heterogeneous 156-qubit heavy-hex superconducting processor by adapting to underperforming components instead of requiring perfect hardware.
engineering_relevance: This shows a practical path to scalable fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computing using processor-aware scheduling, decoding, and post-selection to tolerate real fabrication variability.
method: Dynamic compass code on a 156-qubit heavy-hex lattice
Noise-informed decoding plus exclusion of the worst qubits/couplers
Post-selection on low-leakage shots and exclusive decoding for lattice surgery
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 35% lower logical memory error, up to 56% improvement for measurement-based logic, Bell fidelities above 77% after pre-selection, and above 97% with additional logical-gap post-selection.
watch_item: The gains rely partly on filtering/post-selection, so the effective yield and overhead may limit throughput in full-scale fault-tolerant operation.
paper_title: Error-Corrected Memory and Logic on a Heavy-Hex Superconducting-Qubit Processor
